posts.title: A honey stall joins Row C from 28 November
posts.excerpt: Local producer Linden Honey brings raw regional honey and honeycomb to pitch C7 starting Saturday 28 November.
posts.content:
Beginning Saturday 28 November, visitors to Linden Station Square will find a new regular producer setting out jars along Row C. Linden Honey joins the market roster at pitch C7, bringing raw honey and honeycomb produced entirely within sixty kilometres of Linden Station Square. The addition fills a regular opening in Row C, which brings together regional dairy farmers, cheesemakers, and fruit preserve producers.

The apiary keeps hives across wildflower meadows, clover pastures, and orchard borders along the edge of the regional forest reserve. By keeping all colonies strictly within our sixty-kilometre boundary, Linden Honey ensures that every batch reflects the genuine floral succession of our local countryside, from spring fruit blossoms and summer clover to late autumn heather and ivy nectar. In accordance with Hinata Market principles, the honey is unpasteurized, cold-filtered through fine cloth, and poured into reusable glass jars with plain paper labels.

Joining the market followed our established four-step grower onboarding process. The producer submitted an application, which the market committee reviewed during our monthly review on the first of the month. Grower liaison Amara Osei then visited the apiaries to inspect the extraction shed, verify colony health, and confirm that all packaging met our strict paper and glass standards. Following two trial Saturdays, market manager Ines Valdés confirmed pitch C7 as a regular fixture for the coming season.

Shoppers visiting pitch C7 will find clear seasonal varieties available throughout the coming winter months. The early summer harvest offers a delicate, pale honey dominated by white clover and blackberry bramble blossoms, while the late season extraction yields an amber, rich honey gathered from late summer hedgerows and forest trees. Fresh comb honey will also be cut to order in limited quantities each Saturday morning. Because our six grower rules prohibit wholesale goods and third-party resale, the beekeeper will stand behind the trestle table every week, ready to answer questions about colony management, seasonal foraging, and apiary care.

The arrival of Linden Honey marks an exciting milestone as Hinata Market prepares for its winter schedule. While our operating hours adjust to 09:00 until 13:00 throughout December, January, and February, all forty pitches across Rows A through D remain active. As morning preparation gets underway with Tomas Brandt chalking pitch boundaries at 05:30, crates arriving at 07:40, and the ceremonial bell ringing at 07:55, the square continues to bring honest regional sustenance directly to town.

We invite everyone to visit pitch C7 on Saturday 28 November to welcome our newest grower. Remember to bring your own shopping bags or baskets, as paper wrapping and reusable containers remain standard across all stalls. Card and cash payments are accepted at the stall, ensuring an easy morning checkout whether you are collecting a single jar of comb honey or stocking your pantry for the cold weeks ahead. For more details on weekly stall locations or to check seasonal produce availability before your morning visit, stop by the visitor desk at pitch A1 to speak with Lena Hoffmann, or subscribe to our weekly list sent every Thursday at 18:00.

posts.title: Bicycle parking moves to the east arcade
posts.excerpt: From Saturday 21 November cargo bikes and bicycles park in the east arcade.
posts.content:
From Saturday 21 November, bicycles and cargo bikes park in the covered east arcade, beside the tram stop. The east gate opens at 07:30 for cargo bikes carrying crates.

The racks beside pitch A1 are kept clear for the visitor desk.

posts.title: Soup Saturday on 5 December: bring a bowl
posts.excerpt: A big pot of seasonal soup at 11:00 on 5 December. Bring your own bowl.
posts.content:
On Saturday 5 December a volunteer ladles seasonal soup from a large pot at 11:00. Bring your own bowl and spoon; there are no disposables on the square.

The vegetables come from rows B and D.

posts.title: The knife sharpener is back on the first Saturday of each month
posts.excerpt: Knife sharpening returns to pitch D9 on the first Saturday of each month.
posts.content:
The knife sharpener is back at pitch D9 on the first Saturday of each month. Leave a knife wrapped in cloth and collect it before 14:00.

It is the one stall that sells a service rather than produce, so it sits at the end of Row D.
